newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Former Ivorian chief of staff thrown out of army.
newsitem.headline: Former Ivorian chief of staff thrown out of army.

text.p: Ivory Coast's former army chief of staff, General Robert Guei, sacked amid talk of a coup attempt during the 1995 presidential election, has been thrown out of the armed forces for serious misconduct.

A government statement, read on state television after a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, said President Henri Konan Bedie had signed a decree ejecting Guei from the armed forces following deliberations of a military commission of enquiry.
"This measure comes after the commission of enquiry found that there had been serious faults in the exercise of his duties as chief of staff and serious faults of discipline," the statement said.

Officials said at the time of the election, which Bedie won in the face of bloody political unrest and a boycott by the main opposition, that Guei had refused to order the army onto the streets to help maintain order.
At the time sources close to Guei said he maintained that the army should not become involved in politics.
The hearings of the commission have been shrouded in secrecy, drawing fire from the opposition press.
A handful of junior officers and other ranks, who had been detained in the aftermath of the elections, were thrown out of the army at the end of last year.
Guei, who has never been formally arrested, served in Bedie's government following his election, notably as minister of sport. He was dropped in a subsequent reshuffle.

Guei was appointed by Ivory Coast's independence president Felix Houphouet-Boigny during Ivory Coast's tense transition to democracy in the early 1990s. Bedie took over as Houphouet- Boigny's heir apparent on his death in late 1993.

The political unrest during the October 1995 presidential election, during which 35 people died in political and ethnic clashes, contrasted with the West African nation's tradition of stability in a volatile corner of the world.
